headline_finding: Anna's structural lead over density-matched random PERSISTS at gen-500. Lead narrows from 0.068 (init) to 0.031 (final), then stabilizes from gen-200 onward. After 500 hill-climb mutation cycles, training does NOT erase Anna's prior advantage.
comparison_to_phase_c4: Phase C4 ran 200 generations with the same seeds and reported Anna lead 0.034 at gen-200. Phase D6 reproduces this exactly (0.0324 at gen-200) and shows the lead is asymptotically stable around +0.031.
interpretation: Anna's prior is partially-but-not-fully consumed by training. A lead of +0.031 (≈ 5% relative hit rate advantage) persists at 500 generations, suggesting the structural prior provides genuine optimization benefit beyond what greedy mutation reaches in the same time budget.
